claim_verdicts.suggested_text: Without acceptance criteria two people read the same story two different ways — the team's note says a third reading turns up at testing — so neither a size nor a claim that it is finished means the same thing to both of them.

claim_verdicts.evidence: Scrum Guide 2020, Increment: "Work cannot be considered part of an Increment unless it meets the Definition of Done." — first half exact. But the same section says "Multiple Increments may be created within a Sprint." and "An Increment may be delivered to stakeholders prior to the end of the Sprint." plus "The Sprint Review should never be considered a gate to releasing value." So "the usable piece of product the sprint hands over" (one per Sprint, handed over at its end) is not what the Guide says; only "the Increment must be usable" is.
claim_verdicts.source: https://scrumguides.org/scrum-guide.html — Increment; Commitment: Definition of Done
claim_verdicts.suggested_text: Work that has not passed the checklist cannot be counted part of an Increment — a usable piece of product the team can hand over, and a sprint may produce more than one.

Lines 18-19: "5. Khi tôi hủy cùng một đơn hai lần, lần thứ hai trả về 409 và trạng thái đơn" / "   vẫn là `cancelled`."

Lines 10, 12, 14, 16, 18 each begin "N. Khi …": Khi đơn ở trạng thái `new`…; Khi tôi bấm \"Hủy đơn\" và xác nhận…; Khi đơn ở trạng thái `paid`, `shipped` hoặc `cancelled`…; Khi tôi gọi API…; Khi tôi hủy cùng một đơn hai lần…. Two name a state of the order, three name something the customer does; each is followed by what the system does.

Lines 23-27 verbatim: "- [ ] Code đã được ít nhất một người khác đọc và duyệt." / "- [ ] Có test tự động cho mọi tiêu chí chấp nhận ở trên." / "- [ ] Chạy được trên môi trường thử nghiệm, không chỉ trên máy người viết." / "- [ ] Không thêm cảnh báo mới khi build." / "- [ ] Tài liệu API đã cập nhật." The five glosses match in order.
docs/team/sprint-example.md, "## Retrospective" (line 35), line 37: "- Làm tốt: viết tiêu chí chấp nhận trước khi code, nhờ vậy không phải làm lại." — what went well, plus the reason (no rework).

Scrum Guide 2020, Commitment: Definition of Done: "The Definition of Done is a formal description of the state of the Increment when it meets the quality measures required for the product." The name and the substance are the Guide's.

Scrum Guide 2020: "If the Definition of Done for an increment is part of the standards of the organization, all Scrum Teams must follow it as a minimum." and "If it is not an organizational standard, the Scrum Team must create a Definition of Done appropriate for the product." The Definition is stated once, against the Increment ("a formal description of the state of the Increment"); the Guide attaches it to no individual Product Backlog item.

Fetch of the full 2020 Guide: neither "user story" nor "acceptance criteria" occurs anywhere in the document — first half holds. Second half overstates: the Guide's sentence is "This is an ongoing activity to add details, such as a description, order, and size." "such as" opens the list; the Guide does not say those three are all that refinement adds. (No local mirror of the Guide under refs/, so this rests on a full-text fetch, not a Grep.)
claim_verdicts.source: https://scrumguides.org/scrum-guide.html — Product Backlog; Product Backlog refinement
claim_verdicts.suggested_text: The Scrum Guide 2020 uses neither the term user story nor the term acceptance criteria, and prescribes no format for a Product Backlog item; on refinement it says only that it adds details, such as a description, order and size.

claim_verdicts.evidence: sprint-example.md rows 14-18, last column: Xong, Xong, Xong, "Chưa xong, chuyển sprint sau", Xong. Line 17: "| Ngừng gửi thông báo cho đơn đã hủy | Dev 3 | 2 | Chưa xong, chuyển sprint sau |" — the only unfinished row.

The three repo parts hold: story-example.md 35-36 ("hỏi trước khi code, không phải đoán rồi hy vọng"), sprint-example.md 24 ("cần PO trả lời"), 37 (retro). But the embedded gloss "the product owner, who decides what is wanted" is a role claim about Scrum, filed here as kind `opinion` with no `version_key`. The Guide supports a narrower wording: "The Product Owner is accountable for maximizing the value of the product resulting from the work of the Scrum Team" and for Product Backlog management, including creating and ordering Product Backlog items.
claim_verdicts.source: examples/don-hang @ stage-0 — story-example.md:35-36, sprint-example.md:24,37; https://scrumguides.org/scrum-guide.html — Product Owner
claim_verdicts.suggested_text: Split the ledger entry: keep the team-note part as `opinion`, and file "the product owner is the one accountable for what goes into the product and in what order" as a separate `fact` claim with version_key `scrum`.

issues.text: Unlisted claim: a comparative assertion about document length, in no claim in the ledger and supported by neither the repo note nor any pinned document. The team's note says only that a story is a promise of a conversation and that unclear points are asked about before coding; it says nothing about what long documents do to questions.
issues.quote: It stays short on purpose, because a sentence invites the questions a long document closes off.
issues.fix: Replace with what the note supports: "It stays short on purpose: the note calls the story a promise of a conversation, not a specification, so the questions it leaves open are meant to be asked." Or keep the sentence and add it to .meta.json as an `opinion` claim sourced to story-example.md lines 35-36.

issues.text: Prose overstates criterion 1. Criterion 1 reads "Khi đơn ở trạng thái `new` và thuộc về tôi, … hiện nút" — a condition and what follows from it. It does not say the button appears for nothing else; the exclusivity comes from criterion 3, which the same sentence then credits separately. Claim 9 is filed correctly; only the lesson sentence adds "only".
issues.quote: The first puts the button on the screen only for an order in state `new` that belongs to you; the third hides it for `paid`, `shipped` and `cancelled`.
issues.fix: Drop the misplaced "only": "The first puts the button on the screen for an order in state `new` that belongs to you; the third hides it for `paid`, `shipped` and `cancelled`."

issues.text: The gloss on increment says one per sprint, handed over at its end. Scrum Guide 2020: "Multiple Increments may be created within a Sprint." and "An Increment may be delivered to stakeholders prior to the end of the Sprint." and "The Sprint Review should never be considered a gate to releasing value." The supported part is "In order to provide value, the Increment must be usable."
issues.quote: does not count in the sprint's increment, the usable piece of product the sprint hands over
issues.fix: Write: "cannot be counted part of an increment — a usable piece of product the team can hand over, and a sprint may produce more than one." Update claim 8 in .meta.json to the same wording.

issues.text: The definition bullet gives the Definition of Done to the team as flatly as it gives it a shape ("checklist"). The Guide calls it "a formal description of the state of the Increment when it meets the quality measures required for the product" and says that where the organisation sets one, "all Scrum Teams must follow it as a minimum" — the correction section 5 does make, six paragraphs later.
issues.quote: **Definition of Done** — the team's single checklist of what must be true of any finished piece of work, whatever its story says.
issues.fix: Add the condition at first use: "— this team's single checklist of what must be true of any finished piece of work, whatever its story says (some organisations set the list instead)."

issues.text: "saying only that" closes a list the Guide leaves open. The Guide's sentence is "This is an ongoing activity to add details, such as a description, order, and size" — `such as` gives three examples, not the complete set of what refinement adds.
issues.quote: saying only that adding detail to one over time brings in a description, an order and a size
issues.fix: Write: "saying of refinement only that it adds details, such as a description, an order and a size". Update claim 18 in .meta.json to match.

issues.text: The lesson names the Scrum Guide but never its edition, while `versions_used` pins scrum 2020 and claims 16-18 are all read off the 2020 text. The Definition of Done as a commitment of the Increment, and ownership by the Scrum Team rather than the Development Team, are 2020 wording; a reader holding the 2017 edition finds different words in the place the lesson points at. The prereq lesson does not name the edition either.
issues.quote: The name Definition of Done is the Scrum Guide's — the short document that defines Scrum —
issues.fix: Name the edition once, at that first mention: "The name Definition of Done is the Scrum Guide's — the short document, 2020 edition, that defines Scrum —".

issues.text: A reason is attributed to this team that this team does not give. The repo note explains criteria as what makes the story checkable, and the retrospective gives a different reason for writing them first — "nhờ vậy không phải làm lại" (no rework). "not to grade you afterwards" is the author's framing, in no claim in the ledger.
issues.quote: because their job is to tell you what to build, not to grade you afterwards
issues.fix: Use the team's own reason: "because criteria agreed first are what you build towards, which is why the team's retrospective credits them with not having to do the work twice." Or file it as an `opinion` claim in .meta.json.

junior.reviewer: claude-opus-5 (junior reader simulation, prompt 05, fresh pass; known_vocab = 43 foundation terms + sprint, lesson vocab: user-story, acceptance-criteria, definition-of-done; prereq input: scrum-from-junior-seat five-line summary only)

issues.text: "sprint backlog" is the first technical thing the lesson says, and it is not in my vocabulary: the previous lesson's five-line summary names the sprint, the roles, the daily and the retrospective, but never a backlog. I can work out from the next sentence that it has rows with a title and a number, so I kept reading, but I never learn what the list itself is or who put the rows in it. The diagram's first node and quiz q3's first item both depend on the word.
issues.quote: You take a row from the sprint backlog you read last lesson.
issues.fix: After "sprint backlog" in section 2, add a clause: "the list of work the team took into this sprint".

issues.text: "an order" here cannot mean what "order" has meant in every other sentence of this lesson (đơn hàng: order screen, order state `new`, cancel my own order). I read the phrase three times trying to see how a customer order could be a detail added to a backlog row. I think it means the row's position in the list, but the lesson never uses "order" that way anywhere else, so I am guessing.
issues.quote: saying only that adding detail to one over time brings in a description, an order and a size
issues.fix: Replace "an order" with "a place in the list" in that sentence, so the word "order" keeps one meaning in this lesson.

issues.text: This is the one sentence I had to read three times. "gives it to the team, or to the organisation where the organisation sets one" reads like a slip: I cannot tell whether the Guide hands the checklist to the team, or the team hands it somewhere, and "where the organisation sets one" leaves me unsure which "one" is being set. The point that survives is that the checklist belongs to the team and not to a story, which the paragraph then repeats anyway.
issues.quote: and gives it to the team, or to the organisation where the organisation sets one, rather than to a single story
issues.fix: Split it: "…the state the increment must be in to meet the quality the product requires. It belongs to the team — or to the organisation, if the organisation sets the list — and never to a single story."

issues.text: "naming one" stopped me: the sentence has just been about checklists, stories and backlog rows, and "one" could be any of them. From the second half ("says nothing about cancelling") I decide it means a story, but the pronoun costs a re-read in the hardest paragraph of the lesson.
issues.quote: A checklist applied to every story has nothing to gain from naming one, which is why the one above says nothing about cancelling.
issues.fix: Replace "naming one" with "naming any one story", and "the one above" with "the checklist above".

issues.text: "two people sizing it size different work" uses "size" as a noun-ish verb twice in five words; I parsed it as a typo first. The idea behind it is load-bearing — quiz q6 is entirely about what must exist before the team can say how big the work is — and this half-sentence is the only place the lesson states it.
issues.quote: two people sizing it size different work, and two asked whether it is finished can answer differently
issues.fix: Rewrite as: "two people guessing how big it is are guessing about different work, and two asked whether it is finished can answer differently".

issues.text: I was not told at the daily what the junior was blocked on — my previous lesson's summary only says the sentence naming what blocks you matters. The rest of the sentence lets me reconstruct that the block was about a `shipped` order, so I was not stuck long, but the phrase "the screen half of what blocked the junior" asks me to remember something I was never given.
issues.quote: That third line settles only the screen half of what blocked the junior at the daily in last lesson's sprint note
issues.fix: Name the block in the same sentence: "…of what blocked the junior at the daily last lesson — whether a `shipped` order may be cancelled at all".

issues.text: Step 2 asks me to mark which checklist lines my criteria cover, and the expected result says they cover none. But checklist line 2 is "a test for every acceptance criterion", which is about my criteria, so my instinct was to tick it and then find the expected result disagreeing without telling me why. "Cover" is never defined against the checklist.
issues.quote: Expected result: your three criteria are all about notifications and orders, and cover none of the five checklist lines, which are demanded anyway.
issues.fix: Add one sentence to the expected result: "Line 2 asks for a test per criterion, which is a demand on the work, not something a criterion can state — so it counts as not covered."

issues.text: The correct option turns on "the retrospective", a word the lesson body never uses — section 5 says "When this team looked back at the end of the sprint". All I know of the word is one summary line from last lesson saying a team should not drop it. I picked a anyway because b, c and d are clearly wrong, not because I matched the reason.
issues.quote: True, because criteria agreed first tell you what to build, and the retrospective names writing them before coding as what went well.
issues.fix: In the option, replace "the retrospective" with "the team's look back at the end of the sprint", matching the lesson's own wording.
